stories.title: Kostas and his Computer in Athens
stories.summary: Kostas explores computer hardware in Athens and receives an email from his pen-pal Connor in Ireland.
stories.narrative: Kostas is an eleven-year-old pupil in the 5th grade of primary school in Athens. In his free time, Kostas enjoys working on his desktop computer. His computer setup has a wide flat screen, an optical mouse, a keyboard, and a fast printer. On Friday afternoon, Kostas checks his email. He receives a friendly message from his Irish friend Connor who lives in Dublin. Connor writes that he uses the internet to search for information, talk with friends, and play computer games at the weekend. Kostas prefers sending emails to doing homework!
stories.book_check: Pupil's Book p. 14-15: authentic introductory dialogue and email exchange.

stories.title: Three European Friends Online
stories.summary: Kostas connects with Mark in London and Nadine in Marseilles to discuss their school routines and hobbies.
stories.narrative: On Saturday morning, three European friends meet online to chat on the net. Mark is twelve years old and goes to West Wimbledon Primary School in London. Nadine is twelve years old and studies at a Collège in Marseilles. Kostas joins the chat from Athens. Nadine says she likes going to school and loves to study. Mark says he does not mind studying, but he hates difficult tests and long homework. Kostas laughs and says the only thing he likes about school is spending time in the computer lab. They all agree to chat online again tomorrow.
stories.book_check: Pupil's Book p. 18: authentic multi-speaker dialogue between Kostas, Mark, and Nadine.

stories.title: Friends and Flags Across Europe
stories.summary: Classmates share country names, nationalities, and morning greetings from all across Europe.
stories.narrative: Kostas and his classmates learn about friends living in different European countries. Pablo is from Portugal and he is Portuguese. Svetlana is Russian and lives in Moscow. Hans is Dutch and lives in Holland. Carmen is Spanish, Gunther is German, and Maria is Swiss. Armando lives in Albania and Isabella is Italian. Each pupil displays the colourful flag of their nation and shares a morning greeting in their language, from 'Bonjour' in French to 'Buon giorno' in Italian and 'Dobroye utro' in Russian.
stories.book_check: Pupil's Book p. 19 & Appendix p. 133: European nationalities and multilingual greetings.

stories.title: Discovering the British Isles
stories.summary: Mark gives a guided presentation of the British Isles, London, and the floral symbols of each nation.
stories.narrative: Mark writes a presentation about the British Isles. The British Isles are situated on the west side of Europe and consist of two main islands: Great Britain and Ireland. The United Kingdom includes England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. London is the capital city with over 10 million people. Each country has a proud national flower. The national flower of England is the red rose; for Wales, the bright daffodil; for Scotland, the purple thistle; and for Ireland, the green shamrock. Mark also describes the classic black cabs that drive through London streets.
stories.book_check: Pupil's Book p. 22 & Appendix p. 134: authentic British geography and cultural symbols.

grammar_lab.title: Grammar Lab: Expressing Preferences & Present Simple

rules.usage: Use the -ing form of a verb after 'like', 'enjoy', 'love', and 'hate'.
Use 'prefer' + noun/verb-ing + 'to' + noun/verb-ing to show you like one thing more than another.
examples: We prefer surfing the net to watching television.
I prefer reading books to doing housework.

rules.usage: Use the Present Simple for habits, school routines, and general facts. Add -s or -es for he / she / it.
examples: I always check my email when I get back from school.
Nadine studies at a Collège in Marseilles.
They don't have school on Sundays.

practice_items.sentence: Three pupils in our group enjoy _____ (play) computer games.
practice_items.explanation: After 'enjoy', we always use the verb ending in -ing: enjoy playing.

practice_items.sentence: We prefer sending emails _____ doing homework.
practice_items.explanation: We say 'prefer [thing A] TO [thing B]': prefer sending emails TO doing homework.

practice_items.sentence: Kostas _____ (live) in Athens with his family.
practice_items.explanation: For 3rd person singular (he/she/it), we add -s in the Present Simple: Kostas lives.

practice_items.sentence: Mark and Nadine _____ (not / like) doing difficult tests.
practice_items.explanation: For plural subjects (Mark and Nadine = they), the negative form is 'don't like'.

practice_items.sentence: _____ you have an optical mouse for your computer?
practice_items.explanation: Questions in the Present Simple with 'you' start with 'Do': Do you have...?

practice_items.sentence: Nadine is fond of _____ (surf) the net in her free time.
practice_items.explanation: After the preposition 'of', we use the -ing form: fond of surfing.

dialogue_script.speaker: Mark
dialogue_script.text: That’s great! Three European friends! Greek, French, and English! So, how old are you, Kostas?

dialogue_script.speaker: Kostas
dialogue_script.text: I’m eleven. I’m a pupil in the 5th grade of Primary School.

dialogue_script.speaker: Mark
dialogue_script.text: I see. Well, I’m twelve and I’m a pupil at West Wimbledon Primary School. How about you, Nadine?

dialogue_script.speaker: Nadine
dialogue_script.text: Oh, I’m twelve and I’m a student in the second year of Collège. That’s like your middle school.

dialogue_script.speaker: Nadine
dialogue_script.text: Well, not really Mark. Actually, I like going to school and I love studying.

dialogue_script.speaker: Mark
dialogue_script.text: Well, I don’t really mind studying, Nadine, but I hate tests and homework. How about you, Kostas?

dialogue_script.speaker: Kostas
dialogue_script.text: Hm, the only thing I like about school is spending time on our computers.

true_false_quiz.statement: Kostas is twelve years old and goes to school in London.
true_false_quiz.explanation: False. Kostas is eleven and goes to primary school in Athens. Mark is twelve and lives in London.

true_false_quiz.statement: Nadine loves studying and enjoys going to school.
true_false_quiz.explanation: True. Nadine says: 'Actually, I like going to school and I love studying.'
True. Mark says: 'I hate tests and homework.'

true_false_quiz.statement: Kostas says his favourite thing at school is playing football.
true_false_quiz.explanation: False. Kostas says the only thing he likes about school is spending time on the computers.

definition_challenge.title: Theme Terms: Guess the Word from its Definition
definition_challenge.note: Read the child-friendly clue and guess the target term from Unit 1.

group_a.clue: A board with keys used to write letters and numbers on a computer.
A machine that prints words and colourful pictures on paper.
Small speakers you wear over your ears to listen privately.
A worldwide network that connects computers together.

group_b.clue: The main city where the government of a country works.
A small green plant with three leaves that represents Ireland.
A bright yellow spring flower that is the national symbol of Wales.
A prickly purple plant that is the proud national flower of Scotland.

content_true_false.fact: London is the capital of the United Kingdom and is home to over 10 million people.
content_true_false.explanation: True. London is the capital of the UK and its population is around 10-12 million.

content_true_false.fact: The national flower of England is the yellow daffodil.
content_true_false.explanation: False. The national flower of England is the red rose. The daffodil belongs to Wales.

content_true_false.fact: A computer scanner is used to print pictures onto paper.
content_true_false.explanation: False. A printer prints onto paper. A scanner copies pictures into the computer.

content_true_false.fact: Nadine lives in Marseilles, a city in the south of France.
content_true_false.explanation: True. Nadine says she is from Marseilles in the south of France.

content_true_false.fact: The Republic of Ireland is part of the island of Great Britain.
content_true_false.explanation: False. Great Britain is made up of England, Scotland, and Wales. Ireland is a separate island.

writing_workshop.default_topic: Introducing Myself to an Online Friend

paragraphs.heading: Friendly Greeting & Personal Introduction
paragraphs.guiding_questions: What is your name? How old are you? Where are you from?
paragraphs.sample_starter: Dear Connor, Hello from Greece! My name is Kostas and I am eleven years old.

paragraphs.heading: My School & Daily Routines
paragraphs.guiding_questions: Which grade are you in? What subjects do you study? When does school start?
paragraphs.sample_starter: I am a pupil in the 5th grade of primary school. School starts at 8:15 in the morning.

paragraphs.heading: Free Time, Hobbies & Digital Technology
paragraphs.guiding_questions: What do you like doing in your free time? Do you have a computer?
paragraphs.sample_starter: In my free time, I enjoy playing computer games and chatting with friends on the internet.

paragraphs.heading: Closing & Invitation to Reply
paragraphs.guiding_questions: What would you like to ask your new friend? How do you sign off?
paragraphs.sample_starter: What do you like doing at the weekend? Please write back soon! Best wishes, Kostas.

teacher_notes.title: Vocabulary Note: Collège vs. College
teacher_notes.note: Clarify that in France, 'Collège' refers to lower secondary school (ages 11-15, equivalent to the Greek gymnasium), unlike British or American post-18 tertiary colleges.

teacher_notes.title: Geography of the British Isles
teacher_notes.note: Ensure pupils distinguish between Great Britain (the geographical island with England, Scotland, Wales) and the United Kingdom (the sovereign state including Northern Ireland).

book_checks.title: Collège Terminology Note
book_checks.note: Your book says: 'Nadine is in the second year of Collège'. In France, Collège is lower secondary school for pupils aged 11 to 15, matching Greek Gymnasium.

book_checks.title: United Kingdom vs. Great Britain
book_checks.note: Your book distinguishes Great Britain (geographical island) from the United Kingdom (political state). The UK includes Northern Ireland.
